description: Phase 4: Developer-facing map editor (gated to NODE_ENV=development, tree-shaken from production), 2D map overlay, balance tuning passes, edge case hardening, visual polish, and final quality gate. Depends on PRD-01 (Engine Foundation), PRD-02 (Core Gameplay), PRD-03 (Persistence & Debug) — all complete.

requirements: Every new system or module MUST have a co-located test file. Story is not complete without tests.
Unit tests are the minimum quality bar. `pnpm test` must pass before committing.
The full verification command is: `pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build`.
Balance pass stories (US-307 through US-309): write regression tests that assert the tuned values produce expected outcomes.
Edge case stories (US-310a through US-310c): each edge case MUST have a dedicated test proving the fix.

testPatterns.mapEditor: Test MapEditor.enable()/disable() state transitions. Test getMapData()/loadMapData() round-trip serialization. Mock SceneManager for rendering calls.
testPatterns.navigationOverlay: Test overlay toggle (M key), test that game input is consumed while open. Use mockInputManager.
testPatterns.balancePasses: Write parametric tests verifying config values produce expected physics outcomes (e.g., with jumpImpulse and gravity, player reaches expected apex). These tests catch accidental config regressions.
testPatterns.edgeCases: Each edge case in US-310 should be a test: spawn player at bounds -> verify push-back, dismiss cat under player -> verify safe fall, oxygen -> 0 -> health -> 0 -> verify respawn.

testingDirectives.debugBridge: window.__catHerderDebug is exposed in dev mode (Game.ts). Provides: world, gameState, eventBus, physicsEngine, getPlayerEntity(), getActiveCats(), tick(n) for deterministic physics stepping.
antiPatterns: Do NOT mark a story as passing without `pnpm test` succeeding.
Do NOT write tests that import Three.js or require DOM — use mocks for SceneManager/InputManager.
Do NOT skip edge case tests — each acceptance criterion in US-310 maps to a test case.
Do NOT adjust config values without a test proving the old value was wrong and the new value is correct.

userStories.title: Map editor mode
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to toggle into a map editor mode so I can visually edit maps without writing JSON. This creates the MapEditor.ts class and wires it into Game.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/game/maps/MapEditor.ts with public API: enable(), disable(), isActive(): boolean, getMapData(): MapData, loadMapData(data: MapData).
Ctrl+E toggles map editor mode only when process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' (same guard pattern as DebugMenu in src/game/ui/DebugMenu.ts).

Entering editor mode: game pauses (Game.pause()), camera switches to 'free' mode via CameraController.setMode('free') — CameraController already supports CameraMode = 'follow' | 'free' (see src/game/engine/CameraController.ts).
Exiting editor mode: game resumes (Game.resume()), camera returns to 'follow' mode.
Prominent 'EDITOR MODE' banner visible at all times while editor is active — DOM overlay positioned at top-center of canvas container.
Editor does NOT destroy existing game state — entities persist while editing.
Editor code is gated at construction with process.env.NODE_ENV check so it tree-shakes from production bundles.
Wire MapEditor into Game.ts constructor (after DebugMenu init, same dev-gating pattern) and Game.destroy() (call dispose).
Tests: MapEditor enable/disable state transitions, isActive() correctness, Ctrl+E toggle in dev mode. Use mock objects for SceneManager/CameraController dependencies.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: Follow the exact same dev-gating pattern as DebugMenu (constructor returns early in production, null element refs). CameraController already has setMode('free') and panBy() for WASD panning in free mode. The MapEditor will need a reference to CameraController, InputManager, MapManager, and World.

userStories.title: Map editor — terrain tool palette & placement
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a tool palette to select terrain types and click to place blocks on the map, with ghost preview before placement.
acceptanceCriteria: Side panel (DOM overlay, left side of canvas) with tool palette containing: Grass block, Dirt block, Stone block, Water zone. Each tool is a clickable button showing the terrain type name and a color swatch matching TERRAIN_COLORS in MapManager.ts.
Select tool from palette -> click on map -> terrain block placed at grid-snapped position (1u grid, use Math.round(worldPos.x) and Math.round(worldPos.z)).
Terrain blocks have default height of 1u.
Ghost preview: semi-transparent block follows the mouse cursor at the grid-snapped position before placement. Ghost is visible only while a terrain tool is selected.
Side panel only visible when MapEditor.isActive() is true.
New terrain blocks are added to the internal MapEditor state (not directly modifying MapManager — editor maintains its own MapData that can be exported).
Tests: tool selection state, grid snapping logic (verify Math.round produces correct grid positions), placement adds to internal map data.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: The side panel DOM construction follows the same pattern as DebugMenu._build(). Ghost preview uses SceneManager to create a temporary mesh. Grid snapping: Math.round(worldPos) for 1u grid. InputManager already tracks mouse position and left-click events. SceneManager.screenToWorld() converts mouse coords to world space.

userStories.title: Map editor — terrain selection, editing & water zones
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to select placed terrain blocks, edit their properties, adjust height, delete them, and define water zones by drag.
acceptanceCriteria: Click existing terrain block -> select it -> highlighted border (outline or wireframe overlay) on selected block.
Selected block: side panel shows editable properties — type (dropdown), height (number input: 0.5u to 5u in 0.5u increments), position (read-only display).
Changing properties in side panel immediately updates the block in editor state and visual preview.
Delete key removes selected block from editor state and removes its visual representation.
Water zone: when Water tool is selected, click-drag to define rectangular area. Side panel shows depth input for water zones.
Tests: selection state management, property editing updates internal state, delete removes from state, water zone rectangle calculation from drag start/end points.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: Selection requires raycasting from mouse to identify which editor block was clicked. Height adjustment changes the visual box dimensions. Water zones store as rectangular areas in MapData with type=Water.

userStories.title: Map editor — entity placement
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to place spawn points, resource nodes, and special zones on the map so I can define gameplay elements.
acceptanceCriteria: Entity tools added to palette: Player Spawn, Cat Spawn, Resource Node (Grass/Sticks/Water dropdown), Hidden Terrain Zone, Yarn Pickup.
Player Spawn: only one allowed — placing a new one moves the existing one. Shows as a distinct colored marker (e.g., orange circle matching player color #ff6b35).
Cat Spawn: place multiple, each shows as a small cat icon marker (purple circles).
Resource Node: select type from dropdown in side panel, place on map, configure respawn time in side panel (defaults: Grass 30s, Sticks 45s, Water 60s).
Hidden Terrain Zone: click-drag to define area (same as water zone drag), set height in side panel.
Yarn Pickup: place collectible, set yarn amount in side panel (default 3).
All placed entities show as distinct colored markers (different colors per entity type) visible in editor view.
Tests: player spawn uniqueness constraint (new placement moves old one), entity type properties stored correctly, resource node config defaults.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: Entity placement follows the same grid-snap + click pattern as terrain. Entities are stored separately from terrain in the MapEditor's internal state. SpawnPoint interface already exists in src/game/maps/MapData.ts. Resource node configs should match the values in Game.ts spawnTestMapResourceNodes().

userStories.title: Map editor — move & delete tools
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to move and delete placed objects so I can iterate on map layouts.
acceptanceCriteria: Move tool: click any placed object (terrain block or entity) -> drag to new position -> release to place (grid-snapped to 1u).
Delete tool: click any placed object -> object removed from map editor state and visual representation.
Keyboard shortcuts active only while MapEditor.isActive(): M for move tool, D for delete tool, 1-9 for tool palette selection.
Editor active indicator (EDITOR MODE banner from US-301) prevents confusion with gameplay keybindings — M, D, 1-9 are remapped in editor context only.
Undo is NOT required for MVP (explicitly out of scope).
Tests: move tool updates object position in state, delete tool removes object from state, keyboard shortcut routing (M/D/1-9 only fire in editor mode).
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: Move tool needs visual feedback during drag (object follows mouse at grid-snapped position). Keyboard shortcuts should be handled by MapEditor's own keydown listener that only fires when isActive(). InputManager's existing GameAction bindings for M (ToggleMap) must be suppressed while editor is active.

userStories.title: Map editor — save & load
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to save map layouts as JSON files and load them so maps are portable and version-controlled.
acceptanceCriteria: Save button in editor panel: exports current map state as MapData JSON via browser download dialog (document.createElement('a') + Blob download pattern).
Filename auto-generated: map-[name]-[timestamp].json (name from MapData.name, timestamp as ISO string).

Load button: opens file picker (input type=file accept=.json) -> select JSON -> validate with Zod schema mirroring MapData interface from src/game/maps/MapData.ts -> MapEditor.loadMapData(parsed) -> map rebuilds in editor.
Loaded map replaces current editor map entirely (all editor objects cleared and recreated from loaded data).
'Play' button in editor panel: calls MapManager.loadMap(editorMapData) -> exits editor mode (MapEditor.disable()) -> game resumes on the edited map.
Invalid JSON shows error message in editor panel (red text, does not crash). Zod validation catches missing/invalid fields.
No server upload in MVP — maps live as local files committed alongside code.
Tests: getMapData()/loadMapData() round-trip serialization (save -> load -> identical MapData), Zod schema validates correct data and rejects invalid data, Play button triggers MapManager.loadMap.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: Zod is already a project dependency (used in tRPC layer). The Zod schema should mirror the MapData, TerrainCell, and SpawnPoint interfaces from src/game/maps/MapData.ts exactly. The Play button workflow: getMapData() -> MapManager.loadMap(data) -> disable() -> Game.resume().

userStories.title: 2D map overlay
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see an overhead 2D map so I can orient myself in the world.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/game/ui/NavigationOverlay.ts that renders a 2D map when M key is pressed (gameplay mode only — M is suppressed when MapEditor.isActive() per US-304).
Rendered on a separate HTML5 <canvas> element overlaid on the game canvas (no Three.js involvement). Canvas is 400x400px, centered on screen with semi-transparent dark background.
2D top-down view: terrain cells rendered as colored rectangles — Grass=#4a7c59, Dirt=#8b6355, Stone=#6e7074, Water=#1565c0. Hidden terrain not shown unless currently revealed by Curiosity Cat.
Player icon: colored dot matching character color, with triangle arrow showing facing direction.
Active cats: small colored circles at their world positions.
Resource nodes: small icons distinguishable by color per type (Grass=#7bc67e, Sticks=#8b6355, Water=#4fc3f7).
Map scales terrain grid to fit the 400x400 overlay panel.
Pressing M again or Escape closes the overlay. Game continues running behind the overlay (NOT paused).
Input is consumed by the overlay while open (prevent game movement/actions while map is shown).
Tests: overlay toggle state (open/close on M), terrain-to-pixel coordinate mapping, overlay does not pause game. Verify in browser using dev-browser.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: NavigationOverlay needs read-only access to: MapManager (terrain grid), World (entity positions), and the player entity. It uses Canvas 2D context for all drawing. TerrainType colors match TERRAIN_COLORS in MapManager.ts. The overlay consumes input by stopping event propagation while active.

userStories.title: Movement balance pass
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify and tune all movement values so traversal feels satisfying.
acceptanceCriteria: Walk speed (4.5 u/s) verified in src/game/config.ts — write a test asserting CONFIG.walkSpeed === 4.5.
Acceleration (0.3s) verified — test CONFIG.acceleration === 0.3.
Deceleration (0.2s) verified — test CONFIG.deceleration === 0.2.
Jump apex (1.2u) verified — write parametric test: with gravity=-12 and jumpApex=1.2, verify jumpImpulse === sqrt(2 * 12 * 1.2) ≈ 5.367.
Coyote time (5 frames) verified — test CONFIG.coyoteFrames === 5.
Jump buffer (5 frames) verified — test CONFIG.jumpBufferFrames === 5.
Air control (70%) verified — test CONFIG.airControlFactor === 0.7.
Swimming speeds verified: surface=3.2, dive=2.0, ascend=2.5 — test CONFIG.swimSpeedSurface/Dive/Ascend.
If any value feels wrong during browser testing, adjust in src/game/config.ts with a code comment explaining the rationale for the change.
Tests: parametric config value assertions that catch accidental regressions. Verify in browser using dev-browser.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: The derived jumpImpulse is computed at module load: Math.sqrt(2 * Math.abs(gravity) * jumpApex). Test this derivation. runtimeConfig is a mutable copy for debug — tests should assert against the frozen CONFIG object. Browser verification: use dev-browser to navigate to /play and test movement feel.

userStories.title: Cat balance pass
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify and tune cat costs and effects so each cat feels worth its yarn cost.
acceptanceCriteria: Loaf (1 yarn): verify height from cat definition in src/game/cats/definitions/Loaf.ts. Test stacking 2-3 Loafs reaches expected height.
Zoomies (2 yarn): verify 2x speed multiplier and trail length from src/game/cats/definitions/Zoomies.ts.
Curiosity Cat (2 yarn): verify 5u reveal radius and 20s duration from src/game/cats/definitions/CuriosityCat.ts.
Pounce (3 yarn): verify 3.5u launch impulse from src/game/cats/definitions/Pounce.ts. Total reach = cat height + impulse apex should reliably reach ~3.5u high platforms.
Starting yarn (10) verified — test GameState initial yarn value.
Cat limit (3) verified — test CONFIG.maxActiveCats === 3.
If any value feels wrong during browser testing, adjust in cat definition files with a code comment explaining the rationale.
Tests: regression tests for each cat's key parameters (yarn cost, duration, effect magnitude). Verify in browser using dev-browser — summon each cat type and verify behavior.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: Cat definitions are in src/game/cats/definitions/. Each exports a CatDefinition with type, name, yarnCost, duration, and type-specific parameters. CAT_REGISTRY in src/game/cats/definitions/index.ts maps CatType -> CatDefinition. Use entityFactories.ts helpers for spawning test cats.

userStories.title: Resource balance pass
userStories.description: As a developer, I want resource gathering to hit the GDD feel targets so the core loop is satisfying.
acceptanceCriteria: Grass gather time (1.5s) verified — test the GRASS_CONFIG in Game.ts spawnTestMapResourceNodes (gatherTime: 1.5).
Sticks gather time (1.5s) verified — test STICKS_CONFIG (gatherTime: 1.5).
Water gather time (2.0s) verified — test WATER_CONFIG (gatherTime: 2.0).
Respawn timers verified: Grass (30s), Sticks (45s), Water (60s) — regression tests for respawn values.
Inventory cap (10) verified — test GameState.maxInventoryCapacity === 10. If >20% of test session is inventory management, increase to 15 and document the change.
'+1 Resource' floating text feedback verified — existing VisualEffectsSystem handles this.
If any value feels wrong during browser testing, adjust values and document rationale in code comments.
Tests: regression tests asserting gather time, yield, and respawn for each resource type. Verify in browser using dev-browser — gather each resource type and verify timing feels snappy.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: Resource configs are defined inline in Game.ts spawnTestMapResourceNodes(). Consider extracting to config.ts if values need adjustment — but only if the current structure causes issues. GameState tracks inventory with maxInventoryCapacity.

userStories.title: Edge cases — terrain safety & cat validation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want terrain clipping, boundary violations, and cat summoning edge cases handled gracefully.
acceptanceCriteria: Player cannot get stuck in terrain: if collision detection finds player overlapping terrain geometry, push-out resolution moves player to nearest valid position. Add push-out logic to CollisionSystem or PhysicsEngine.
Player cannot walk out of map bounds: boundary walls already exist (MapManager.createBoundaryWalls), verify they block movement at all map edges.

Cat cannot be summoned inside collision geometry: CatCompanionManager.summon() already validates position via isValidPosition() — enhance with auto-raise: try up to 3 y-positions (0.5u increments above requested position), fail with user feedback if all 3 fail.

Cat dismissed while player is standing on it: player falls safely with no void/clip. Verify PhysicsEngine handles the sudden removal of support surface gracefully (player enters airborne state and lands on ground below).

Tests: dedicated test per edge case — spawn player at terrain overlap position and verify push-out, attempt summon inside geometry and verify auto-raise or failure feedback, dismiss loaf cat under player and verify safe landing.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: CollisionSystem is in src/game/systems/CollisionSystem.ts. PhysicsEngine handles ground detection via raycasting. CatCompanionManager.isValidPosition() checks terrain validity. The Loaf cat is the primary 'stand on' cat — use it for the dismiss-while-standing test. Existing integration test in src/game/__tests__/integration/loaf-platform.test.ts may need extension.

userStories.title: Edge cases — death respawn & inventory
userStories.description: As a developer, I want death respawn, inventory-full feedback, and swimming save/load to work correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Oxygen draining to 0 -> health draining to 0: player respawns at map spawn point with full health (5 hearts) and full oxygen — no death screen, no health penalty (Zen Engagement pillar). Add respawn logic: when PlayerControlled.health reaches 0, teleport to spawn point, reset health to maxHealth (5), reset oxygen to 100%.

Inventory full -> gathering attempt: clear feedback message shown to player ('Inventory Full' text overlay), gathering does not start. GatheringSystem should check inventory capacity before beginning gather.

Saving while swimming: on load, if player position is in water zone, SwimmingState is correctly applied. Verify Persistence.restoreFromSave() checks terrain at loaded position and adds SwimmingState component if in water.

Tests: oxygen=0 -> health=0 -> verify respawn at spawn point with full stats. Inventory at max -> attempt gather -> verify rejection with feedback. Save in water -> load -> verify SwimmingState component exists.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: OxygenSystem (src/game/systems/OxygenSystem.ts) already drains health when oxygen=0. Death respawn needs to hook into the health-reaches-0 condition. Existing swimming-oxygen integration test: src/game/__tests__/integration/swimming-oxygen.test.ts. GatheringSystem is in src/game/systems/GatheringSystem.ts — check isInventoryFull() before starting gather. SpawnPoint with role='player' defined in TestMap.

userStories.title: Edge cases — input stability & cleanup
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rapid input, tab unfocus, and HMR/route-change edge cases handled without crashes or leaks.
acceptanceCriteria: Rapid input: holding multiple keys, mashing jump, spam-clicking cat summon produces no crashes or inconsistent state. Verify all input handlers are idempotent and state transitions are guarded.

Tab unfocus: game pauses naturally (requestAnimationFrame stops when tab is hidden). Auto-save beacon fires via beforeunload (already implemented in PRD-03 US-203 Persistence.setupBeforeUnload()). Verify no errors on focus return.

HMR / route change: navigating from /play to / and back leaks no WebGL contexts. Game.destroy() already disposes all modules — verify SceneManager.dispose() releases renderer, and no orphaned event listeners remain. Check WebGLRenderer disposal in src/game/engine/SceneManager.ts.

Tests: rapid input simulation (fire multiple simultaneous key events + clicks, verify no thrown exceptions). Tab visibility change simulation (document.hidden mock, verify game loop stops/resumes cleanly). Verify Game.destroy() cleans up all registered event listeners and WebGL resources.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: InputManager.ts already handles rapid input by using Sets for held/pressed keys (inherently deduplicating). CatPlacementSystem guards against rapid clicks with cooldowns. Game.destroy() calls dispose() on all modules. The beforeunload beacon is set up by Persistence.setupBeforeUnload() — already tested in src/game/__tests__/api/beacon-save.test.ts.

userStories.title: Visual polish — environment
userStories.description: As a developer, I want environment visual refinements that make the world feel more alive.
acceptanceCriteria: Ground plane shadows: player and cat entities cast elliptical shadow sprites onto ground plane. Implement as flattened dark circles (Three.js PlaneGeometry with shadow texture/dark circle material) parented to each entity, positioned at ground level.

Terrain grid lines: subtle grid overlay on terrain for spatial reference. Implement as a GridHelper or custom line geometry at y=0.01 (slightly above terrain surface). Grid spacing matches cellSize (2u for TestMap).
Terrain color variation: slight random tint per terrain cell within type — not all grass identical green. Apply small HSL lightness variation (±5%) seeded by cell position for deterministic results.
Water zone: semi-transparent blue with subtle animation. Implement opacity pulse (oscillating between 0.6-0.8 alpha) or UV shift on water terrain entities. Update in VisualEffectsSystem.update().
Tests: verify shadow entity creation per player/cat, grid dimensions match map size, color variation produces different-but-similar colors per cell. Verify in browser using dev-browser.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: VisualEffectsSystem (src/game/systems/VisualEffectsSystem.ts) already runs per frame and has access to SceneManager. RenderSystem (src/game/systems/RenderSystem.ts) creates meshes from Renderable components. Shadows can be implemented as additional child meshes. Water animation can modify material opacity via SceneManager API. TestMap cellSize=2, size 30x30 grid.

userStories.title: Visual polish — entity effects
userStories.description: As a developer, I want entity-related visual effects that make interactions feel more alive.
acceptanceCriteria: Cat summon effect: brief scale-up animation (0 -> 1 over 0.2s) when a cat is summoned. Listen for 'cat:summoned' event on EventBus, apply scale tween to the cat's mesh.
Cat dismiss effect: brief scale-down animation (1 -> 0 over 0.2s) when a cat is dismissed. Listen for 'cat:dismissed' event, apply scale tween then destroy entity after animation completes.

Gather progress: smooth progress bar animation (lerp current width toward target, no jerky step increments). Modify the existing gather progress display in HUD/UIManager to use CSS transitions or requestAnimationFrame interpolation.

Hidden terrain reveal: shimmer/fade-in transition when Curiosity Cat reveals hidden terrain. Currently CuriositySystem sets opacity from 0 to 1 instantly — change to a 0.5s fade-in transition using VisualEffectsSystem.

Tests: verify cat summon triggers scale animation (check transform scale changes over time), gather progress interpolation produces smooth values, hidden terrain opacity transitions from 0 to 1 over expected duration. Verify in browser using dev-browser.
pnpm test && pnpm typecheck passes.
userStories.notes: EventBus already emits 'cat:summoned' and 'cat:dismissed' events (see src/game/types.ts GameEvent union). CuriositySystem (src/game/systems/CuriositySystem.ts) currently calls SceneManager.setMeshOpacity() directly — refactor to use a tween tracked by VisualEffectsSystem. GatheringSystem.getGatherState() returns current progress percentage for the HUD.

userStories.title: Final quality gate
userStories.description: As a developer, I need all quality checks passing so the MVP vertical slice is shippable.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm lint passes with zero warnings.
pnpm typecheck passes with zero errors.
pnpm build succeeds and produces an optimized bundle.
No console errors on clean startup of /, /play, or the auth callback route.
No console warnings related to game logic (Three.js deprecation warnings are acceptable).
Game maintains 60 FPS with test map fully populated (all resource nodes, 3 active cats, swimming active) — verify via debug menu Session tab FPS counter.
Auth flow completes: sign in -> /play, sign out -> /, refresh -> session persists via WorkOS cookies.
Save/load round trip verified: play -> close tab -> reopen -> state matches (position, yarn, inventory, active cats).
All 4 cat types functional: Loaf (platform), Zoomies (speed), CuriosityCat (reveal), Pounce (launch).
Swimming + oxygen verified: enter water, dive, surface, oxygen drains/refills correctly.
Debug menu functional (Ctrl+D opens, all tabs work) and stripped from production bundle — grep production JS output for 'DebugMenu' identifier, should not appear.
Map editor produces valid MapData (save -> load -> identical map) and is similarly stripped from production bundle — grep for 'MapEditor' in production JS.
Verify in browser using dev-browser: run full test scenario covering all features.
pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build all pass.
userStories.notes: This is a verification-only story — no new features, only fixing issues discovered during the quality gate checks. If lint/typecheck/build fail, fix the issues. If production bundle contains debug code, verify the process.env.NODE_ENV gating is correct. Production build output is in .next/ directory (Next.js).
